blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-1 (Unbounded retry of a non-idempotent charge can bill an order several times) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-2 (The payment call has no timeout and can hang the checkout path) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-3 (Payment failures are swallowed without any log) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Bound the retries (a few attempts with exponential backoff and jitter) and retry only errors that are safe to repeat: connection errors before the request was sent, 429 and 5xx — never 4xx such as a declined card or a bad amount, which today loop forever. Make the POST idempotent by sending an idempotency key derived from the order (e.g. an `Idempotency-Key: <order_id>` header, if the provider supports it) so a retry after a read timeout or a 5xx that was in fact processed does not create a second charge. After the last attempt, raise an error naming the order and the provider status.
findings.title: Unbounded retry of a non-idempotent charge can bill an order several times

findings.recommendation: Pass an explicit `timeout=` (connect and read, e.g. `timeout=(3, 10)`) to `requests.post`, and treat a read timeout as an outcome of unknown state — retried only with the idempotency key of R-ops-1.
findings.title: The payment call has no timeout and can hang the checkout path

findings.recommendation: Log each failed attempt with structured fields — `order_id`, attempt number, HTTP status or exception class, provider error code — at warning level, and at error level when giving up; never log the request body beyond the order and amount. Consider a counter metric of charge attempts and failures by outcome so a provider outage is visible on a dashboard.
findings.title: Payment failures are swallowed without any log

findings.recommendation: Read the provider URL from the environment or the application's configuration (e.g. `PAYMENT_URL = os.environ["PAYMENT_URL"]`), so staging and tests target the sandbox and production the live endpoint.
findings.title: The provider URL is hard-coded instead of read from configuration
